title: New Toyota Fortuner Spied Testing in Argentina Ahead of December Debut
excerpt: Spy photographs near Toyota's Zárate plant show a comprehensive facelift for the SUV sold locally as the SW4, with an India launch expected in 2027 but not yet confirmed by Toyota.
body:
• A camouflaged updated Toyota Fortuner has been photographed testing in Argentina, near the Zárate plant where the SUV is built for South America.
  • Reports describe a comprehensive facelift rather than a new generation: the IMV ladder-frame platform and core bodyshell are expected to carry over, with sharper styling and a longer equipment list.
  • The global debut is scheduled for December 1 in South Africa, according to Rush Lane and CarBike360, and an India launch is expected in 2027.
  • For buyers in India: Toyota has not confirmed an India launch date, specifications or prices for the updated model. The current Fortuner remains on sale, including the Leader Edition launched in October at Rs 36.51 lakh to Rs 38.72 lakh ex-showroom.

Toyota's updated Fortuner has been spotted on road tests in Argentina, the latest sighting of the SUV ahead of a global debut that Rush Lane reports is scheduled for December 1 in South Africa. In Argentina and Brazil the Fortuner is sold as the SW4; all South American units are built at Toyota's Zárate plant in Argentina, near where the test vehicle was photographed.

What the spy shots show

The camouflaged vehicle shows sharper lighting elements and a mesh-style grille, design details that resemble the ninth-generation Hilux launched earlier this year, according to Rush Lane. The test vehicle also appears to have a more upright stance, with a reworked air intake and front bumper, though finer details are hidden by the camouflage.

Side changes are expected to be limited, possibly including new alloy wheels. Earlier spy photographs, reported by both Rush Lane and CarBike360, showed revised tail lamps, a connected LED light bar and a redesigned tailgate at the rear.

A facelift, not a new generation

Both publications describe a comprehensive facelift built around the existing architecture: the IMV ladder-frame platform and core bodyshell are expected to carry over, with changes to exterior design, cabin and equipment.

Inside, the updated Fortuner is expected to get a redesigned steering wheel and new instrument cluster and infotainment system, with possible additions to its driver-assistance package. Rush Lane reports some equipment may be shared with the new Hilux, with further features possibly borrowed from the Tacoma, currently sold only in North America. Toyota has confirmed none of these details.

Engines: what is expected for India

For the Indian market, the new Fortuner is expected to continue with the existing 2.8-litre diesel engine, with the current manual and automatic transmission options carried over, according to Rush Lane. The publication adds that Toyota could also reintroduce a 2.7-litre petrol engine option, in the context of stricter emission norms. CarBike360 likewise expects the 2.8-litre diesel to continue, noting Toyota has not confirmed the India model's engine lineup or specifications.

What it means for buyers

In Argentina, the updated SW4 is expected to launch in 2027 initially in a single SRX variant, with Diamond and GR-Sport variants to follow, according to Rush Lane. For India, both publications put the launch in 2027 with no narrower window, and Toyota Kirloskar Motor has announced no date.

Until the December 1 debut, every detail beyond the spy photographs themselves — styling, equipment, engines and timing — remains expectation rather than confirmed specification. Buyers who need an SUV now are choosing from the current range: Toyota's most recent India addition is the 2026 Fortuner Leader Edition, announced on October 9 with 4x2 manual and automatic variants priced at Rs 36,51,000 and Rs 38,72,000 ex-showroom, bookable through Toyota's website and dealerships. The December debut should replace spy-shot guesswork with the production model's actual design and equipment.
